chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had some dinars with me, and he was ill. He said to me, 'If a death occurs to me, give so-and-so twenty dinars, and give my brother the remainder of the dinars.' He died, and I did not witness his death. Then a truthful Muslim man came to me and said to me, 'Indeed, he ordered me to tell you: Look at the dinars that I ordered you to give to my brother, and give charity from them with ten dinars, distribute them among the Muslims.' His brother did not know that I had anything, so he said, 'I think you should give charity from them with ten dinars, as he said.'

key_terms.مَرِيضٌ: A person in their final illness (marḍ al-mawt)

ai.seo_question: How is a supplementary charitable instruction from the deceased handled if it affects a beneficiary's share of the estate?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'Wasiyya al-Ziyada' (supplementary bequest), where a custodian can execute a later instruction from the deceased even if the primary beneficiary is unaware. It highlights the validity of conditional or supplementary directives in wills, emphasizing the custodian's duty to verify and implement the deceased's final wishes regarding charitable distribution.
